brief: Jackie Leven 2006. Zwei eigenständige Kompositionen mit wiedererkennbaren Gesichtszügen. Stil und Helligkeit folgen ausdrücklich der vom Nutzer bevorzugten zurückgenommenen Fassung.

variants.title: Offener Blick
variants.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: one portrait artwork for a Jackie Leven tribute website, his 2006 life phase, continuing an approved series.
INPUT ROLES:
Images 1, 2 and 3: facial identity, age and build references for Jackie Leven in 2006. Study this older, heavyset man precisely: broad rounded face, full cheeks and substantial lower face and neck, distinctive eyes and lids, nose and mouth, slightly receding thick wavy medium-length hair, naturally mature clean-shaven face. Preserve his actual recognizable facial proportions and substantial body. He is in his mid-fifties here, neither the slim youth nor a very elderly man.
Image 4: STYLE AND TONAL REFERENCE ONLY, the approved earlier-period artwork. Match its restrained dark matte-gray dry-brush-on-anthracite language. DO NOT copy the young man's facial anatomy, slender body, hairstyle or specific pose from image 4.
Create an independently composed illustration of the man in images 1-3. The user expressly permits a new layout, pose, body language, light and ambiance. Do not trace or reproduce any source photograph's scene, angle, microphone geometry, stage arrangement, lighting or crop. Remove all source-photo stage equipment, tent poles, badges, lanyards, shirt patches and colored stage lights.
Style/medium: markedly abstracted rough dry-brush ink painting, graphite-gray pigment on deep anthracite #0d0f12. Follow image 4 in economy and darkness. A small number of broad matte gray masses describe the face, with a few precise eye, nose, mouth and jaw marks retaining identity. Broken dry bristle edges and open contours; individual brush strokes visible. No photographic gradients, realistic skin texture, detailed engraving or smooth airbrushing. Do not deform or beautify facial anatomy for expressiveness.
TONAL INVARIANTS: the user's explicitly selected direction is the darker, understated image 4. Most of the whole image is near-black. Use charcoal #30373c, mid-dark slate #444b50, restrained facial planes #60676a; only small facial accents up to #73797b. No white, silver glow, pale shirt or bright face. Clothing merges almost entirely into background. Eyes/pupils, nostrils and mouth line remain naturally dark inside lighter facial planes, never invert them.
Vertical 4:5. The head remains large enough to read beside website text. The outer 4–7% edges fade into uniform #0d0f12, no rectangular art border or contrasting paper. Dark gaps and spare edge strokes make the silhouette dissolve organically into the site. No lettering, logos, symbols, signature, watermark text or extra people. Match the approved artwork's quiet tonal presence and physical, unsentimental brushwork.

COMPOSITION A — CLOSE PORTRAIT, OPEN GAZE:
New chest-up portrait with the torso slightly turned toward the viewer's right, head turned back subtly toward the viewer's left, face near eye level, eyes open and looking just off camera as if listening between songs. Closed mouth, a subtle relaxed asymmetry around its corners rather than a broad smile, alert and grounded presence. Shoulders relaxed, full neck and lower face faithful to the 2006 man. Dark open-collar plain shirt with rolled fabric suggested by a few strokes. No hands, guitar or microphone in this close crop.
Keep complete crown of hair and enough dark margin. A restrained band of side light reveals forehead, cheek, nose and a little collar. Hair is a few broad wavy brush masses. The rest is pure abstract darkness, no literal room, ornamental brush halo or invented props. Mature physical presence and warmth without becoming sentimental or polished.

COMPOSITION B — SEATED WITH A GUITAR, A NEW QUIET MOMENT:
Compose a new medium portrait from upper torso to just below the guitar's upper bout. He sits with a grounded, slightly forward-leaning posture, chest almost facing the viewer, head rotated gently toward the viewer's right and angled down only slightly. His eyes are partially open, focused beyond the instrument, mouth closed as if between lines. Keep his full rounded face readable in a gentle three-quarter view and his substantial torso faithful.
An acoustic guitar rests low across his lap, largely dissolving into shadow. One relaxed forearm rests over the guitar's upper edge; a hand is loosely draped beside the soundhole, correctly drawn, simplified and subordinate. The neck runs diagonally toward the lower right edge, mostly disappearing. Compose this from scratch: no exact pose or hand placement from a source photo. No microphone or stand. The guitar is indicated by just a broken gray outer curve, a suggestion of soundhole and a few economical neck/strings marks, not a bright wooden object.
Plain dark open-neck shirt. The background is abstract dark atmosphere without a venue or scenery. A narrow, muted side light links face, a small part of the forearm and the guitar curve; the face is the clearest element and occupies roughly a third of the image height. Everything below the chest gets progressively more incomplete. This is a human, physical musician in a quiet interval, not a generic stage publicity photo.
